---
title: "Merge positional saliva measurements"
output: html_document
---

Laboratory data often identify canonical day and sample position rather than a
physical tube. Positional matching resolves those keys through the
registration-aware Study Results.

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(carwatch)

study_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "carwatch-gallery-merge-saliva")
generate_synthetic_study_data(
  study_dir,
  n_participants = 3,
  missing_awakening_time_ratio = 0,
  missing_sampling_time_ratio = 0,
  random_state = 42,
  create_cortisol_data = TRUE,
  overwrite = TRUE
)

folders <- list.dirs(file.path(study_dir, "logs"), recursive = FALSE, full.names = TRUE)
participant_dirs <- stats::setNames(folders, basename(folders))
study_results <- convert_raw_logs(
  read_raw_logs_from_participant_dirs(participant_dirs),
  errors = "raise"
)
```

```{r merge}
cortisol <- readr::read_csv(
  file.path(study_dir, "cortisol.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

merged_results <- merge_saliva(
  study_results,
  cortisol,
  match_on = "position"
)

head(as_sample_events(merged_results)[, c(
  "participant", "day", "sample", "sample_position", "condition", "cortisol"
)])
```

For a BioPsyKit-style laboratory file keyed by physical tube ID, use
`read_saliva()` and `match_on = "sample"`. CARWatch never infers position from
the spelling of an identifier.
